terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

structureKind: single continuous swept band, not an assembly of discrete parts
constant-topology cross-section that scales along the sweep
multi-ply lamination running parallel to the sweep surface
one through-hole formed by the coil cavity
motionPotential: slow axial roll about the coil axis
per-ply delamination shear along the spar
particulate shedding from the frayed upper edge
materialFamilies: dark stratified composite substrate (very low albedo, matte)
warm ochre oxide staining concentrated in erosion zones
objectClass.notes: Identity is carried by the SPIRAL SWEEP plus the LAMINATION, not by a parts assembly. The single view hides the far side of the coil and the underside of the spar; both are inferred, flagged low confidence.

reasoning: Low part count but very high sweep and surface complexity: one continuous ribbon carries all identity.
Repetition density is the dominant driver — the ply lamination is a many-instance system, and the hull plating is a second grid system.
Occlusion risk is high: a single view shows one face of the coil only.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Observed structure is a swept multi-ply ribbon with dense micro detail. A single extruded band with one material would lose the lamination, which is the object's identity-defining feature.

detailInventory.note: Enumerated from five zoom crops (tail tip, tail mid, outer band, inner wall, coil bottom) cut from remnant-isolated-crop.png.

details.description: Rectangular hull plating across the bright outer face: long thin panels, roughly 4:1 to 12:1 aspect, aligned to the sweep direction, with occasional cross-breaks.
Hairline scribe lines finer than the panel breaks, drawing sub-divisions and occasional diagonal ticks inside panels.
Fine concentric striations on the coil's inner wall — the ply stack seen edge-on. Spacing tightens toward the cavity.
Plies separating and shearing past one another along the spar's lower edge, producing stepped overlapping tongues.
Spalled chips and detached flakes along the spar's frayed upper edge, decreasing in size toward the tip.
The coil's outer rim turns over from the bright plated face to the dark side wall along a narrow eased edge.
Narrow polished highlight riding the outer rim where erosion has worn the plating smooth — the only low-roughness zone on the object.
Warm ochre/rust oxide wash concentrated in the delamination gaps and around spall sites; absent on intact plating.
The coil cavity is a true through-hole, confirmed by the depth map reading it as far-field, not a dark surface.
Small raised greeble clusters — grouped boxy protrusions breaking the plating plane, densest near the coil shoulder.
Directional abrasion streaks running parallel to the sweep across the plated face, consistent with travel through a particle field.
The ply stack's silhouette contour on the coil's shadowed flank, where individual laminae read as stacked arcs against the cavity.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Ribbon cross-section is rectangular with eased long edges (plate cannot resolve chamfer vs fillet).
Far side of the coil mirrors the visible near side. Confidence 0.45.
Spar underside mirrors the plated top face with heavier delamination. Confidence 0.40.
Turn count is 1.4; evidence is the inner terminus arc only. Confidence 0.55.
Ply count 28 is read off the striation spacing on the cavity wall, not counted exactly.

coordinateFrame.front: the plated face of the coil, facing camera-right and slightly up
coordinateFrame.up: image up; the coil axis is tilted ~20 degrees off the view axis

silhouette.boundingShape: A comma or apostrophe: a thick near-circular coil at lower-right with a long tapering spar sweeping up-left at roughly 28 degrees above horizontal.
silhouette.symmetry: none — a chiral spiral. Mirroring the model is a hard failure.
dominantCurves: the spiral spine, radius decaying ~0.50 -> 0.19 over ~1.4 turns
the near-straight upper edge of the spar, slightly convex
the concave underside where the spar meets the coil shoulder
negativeSpaces: the coil cavity — a true through-hole, ~0.44 of coil diameter, offset up-left of the coil centre because of the viewing angle
the wedge of empty space between the spar's underside and the coil's upper-left flank

componentTree.name: Remnant Structure 07LF
componentTree.topologyRationale: One continuous ribbon swept along a logarithmic spiral. Reading outward-to-inward: the spar enters top-left, broadens, then winds ~1.4 turns clockwise into the coil. The arm and the coil are the SAME sweep at different arc lengths — they are not attached parts, which is why no attachment contract is declared between them.

collider.notes: Compound proxy: one cylinder for the coil, one tapered capsule for the spar.

repetitionSystems.name: Ply lamination stack
repetitionSystems.notes: The identity-defining system. Each ply is the same sweep offset along the ribbon normal, with jittered arc endpoints so the stack frays unevenly. Plies terminate progressively toward the spar tip, which is what produces the fray without modelling it explicitly.

repetitionSystems.name: Hull plating grid
repetitionSystems.notes: Panels follow the sweep; cross-breaks are stochastic so the grid never reads as tiled.

proceduralStrategy: Build the spiral spine first as a CatmullRom curve; everything else rides it.
Sweep one ply as a tapered rectangular section along the spine, then instance it 28x along the ribbon normal with jittered arc endpoints.
Terminate plies progressively toward the spar tip so the fray emerges from the lamination system rather than being modelled.
Carve the cavity by construction (the sweep never crosses it), never by boolean.
Add plating relief and greebles only after the sweep silhouette passes review.
Keep the ply-index parity tonal alternation — it is what makes the stack legible.
Materials: bone plating and dark substrate are independent; do not share a height field.

component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry

risks.note: Roughly half the coil surface is never observed; any orbit past ~25 degrees shows invented geometry.

Camera-matched projection holds only near the reference viewpoint. ADR-027 measured ~2.5 degrees for the depth-relief treatment on this same plate; real geometry should do better but the limit must be measured, not assumed.
The frayed dissolving edge is the object's identity and cannot be reached by primitives alone; it is delegated to a particle layer outside this spec.
